answer: An agent economy can blunt sybils with a refundable per-identity stake plus attestation paid only to peers closer than a random reference point. Each new agent posts collateral; the ledger picks a random beacon and rewards verifiers whose signed signal sits nearer it than the claimant's. One operator splitting into many cheap identities gains nothing: the clones vouch for each other and forfeit their stakes, while honest nodes earn a steady lotus of fees. Forging N identities costs roughly N times the bond, so the attacker's expected loss grows with every clone before any payout clears.
